printf '%s\n' '# Link and delivery contract

The request uses the actor_id and customer_id fields. A verified receipt is an opaque reference to the original request record. Keep the scope docs_only for callers with no account link. A data-tool attempt returns scope_denied before any tool executes.

A link generation is the version of an account link. After logout retires that generation, dispatch, token exchange and pre-send checks return invalidated; otherwise a channel-policy exclusion returns context_forbidden. Check invalidated first when both apply. Expiry is five minutes from setup creation, not the last retry.

Refresh uses its own version and cannot restore a retired link. Raw credentials remain broker-owned. Runtime tests use fixtures. Staff callers have no extra Customer permission.

Document this behavior without choosing an unapproved provider schema, adding components or implementing a plan.' > source.md
git add source.md && git commit -q -m 'security contract'

printf '%s
' '# Customer Slack authorization

The local test setup starts mocks for the customer-facing Slack app, the internal Sumac app and internal egress.

Regardless of environment, a valid delegation token issued for Trellis customer tier must never authorize Sumac or internal-only tools. The local mocks let the acceptance suite exercise this boundary. Internal egress rejects the token with status 401 and an access log response_code_details beginning jwt_authn_access_denied. No policy-decision log is written and no internal tool receives the request. A valid Sumac-internal request remains permitted.

Real-provider deployment is outside this milestone. The customer-tier authorization behavior is proposed.' > source.md
